newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia dlr dead in the water after setback.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia dlr dead in the water after setback.

text.p: The Australian dollar drifted higher through a very subdued Friday session but was still down on the levels seen before the local holiday.

The currency had risen steadily to flirt with 80 cents on Tuesday but lacked the momentum to clear that chart barrier and quickly succumbed to profit-taking. It was quoted as low as US$0.7912/17 during the rarified conditions of Cristmas Day but more liquid trading today saw it recover above US$0.7950.
Bulls were aided in this by the strength of US$/yen, which was testing 44-month highs atop 115.00 yen, and looked set to test the upside once again in the short term.

By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the dollar had dropped anchor at US$0.7960/65 after drifting up from an early US$0.7952/57, but was still well down on the US$0.7991/96 level held when local trade finished on Tuesday.

The seesaw action was taken by traders as outlining a short term trading range from US$0.7910/20 support to 80 cent resistance which could easily last until the new year given how thin turnover was likely to be.
Past that, a break of US$0.7850 or US$0.8050 was needed to establish the medium term direction with the former targetting 77 cents and the latter US$0.8212.
On the crosses, the dollar extended a pre-Xmas rally to reach 91.50/60 yen from 91.30/40 late here Tuesday, emboldened by the U.S. dollar's assault on the 115.00 yen barrier.
The U.S. currency was hovering at 114.95/05 late here Friday having crept up from 114.30/35 over the holiday and touched a fresh 44-month high at 115.08 at one stage.
The yen's weakness largely reflected a market belief that Japanese interest rates were set to remain at record lows for some months to come.
In trade weighted terms the A$ was down 0.1 point at 59.3.
